event.hypothesis: The robust-domain PA-BPE candidate loses its fairness advantage relative to Classical BPE on a genuinely unseen literary work.
event.interpretation: The predicted universal fairness loss was not observed: robust_domain improves balance on Poe but is worse on Alice and pays a cost penalty. With one work per split this is descriptive evidence only; the earlier row-offset Books conclusion is not stable under correct work isolation.
event.next_action: Retrieve several additional complete three-language works, freeze work-level development and confirmation partitions, and compare book-macro Gini, worst-language cost and total cost before designing a positive-dev-gain selector.
event.prediction: On a whole-work-isolated confirmation set, robust_domain will have Gini no lower than Classical BPE and will not improve worst-language token cost.
event.reason: Tested the active cross-domain robustness hypothesis on native whole-work-separated Books data and retained the non-dominating, mixed result.
event.result: On Alice development, robust_domain Gini was 0.013865 versus Classical 0.002063. On Poe confirmation, robust_domain Gini was lower, 0.003492 versus 0.007505, but its worst-language cost was 61.708 versus 61.477 and total language-mean cost was 122.561 versus 121.136.
